text:
Filip Hronek's job in Vancouver is to soak up minutes. He averages 26.31 a night, 27.12 over his last ten, and hit 31.2 in the loss to Philadelphia, all for a team that has lost nine of its last ten. He has 13 points in 21 games, 12 of them assists and eight on the power play, and Vancouver Hockey Daily marked his 300th career point this month.

The scoring is about where it should be: his rate (1.41 points per 60) sits in the middle of our talent range, and one goal on 1.58 expected is a small gap. At five-on-five Vancouver gets 37.9% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, about three points worse than without him, and he has blocked 42 shots. Evolving-Hockey's read on last season adds context: 1.6 wins above replacement, 41st among 215 defensemen, mostly from the power play, with teammates in the bottom 6%. The thing to watch is him jumping in. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 25% of his shots coming off the rush, against 17% for a typical defenseman. He has one point in his last five games.
headline: Filip Hronek soaks up minutes on a sinking team
